description.narrative:
The overall goal is to strengthen the capacity and coordination of the women's movement in Rwanda for more strategic interventions to enhance women's voice and participation, freedom from violence and full enjoyment of human rights.
This goal is aimed to be achieved through the following pathways:
Objective 1: Partners organisations are stronger, more effective and work more strategically and collaboratively
Objective 2: Improved protection from gender based violence with a specific focus on prevention
Objective 3: Rights holders and duty bearers have an increased understanding and respect for Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR)
Objective 4: Enhanced qualitative participation of women in decision making and conflict resolution.

Det övergripande målet för insatsen är att bidra till att stärka kvinnorörelsens kapacitet i Rwanda för mer strategiskt arbete för att förbättra kvinnors röst och deltagande, frihet från våld och fulla åtnjutande av mänskliga rättigheter.
Kvinna till Kvinna har verkat i Rwanda sedan 2017, då ambassaden beslutade att finansiera Kvinna till Kvinnas första landprogram i Rwanda. Programmets övergripande mål har varit att bidra till en starkare och mer samverkande kvinnorättighetsrörelse i Rwanda samt att arbeta mer effektivt för jämställdhet och kvinnors egenmakt. Det nya programförslaget för 2021 - 2024 bygger på framgångar, utmaningar och lärdomar från den nuvarande fasen, samtidigt som fokus flyttas för att svara på socioekonomisk och politisk utveckling för att bättre svara på kvinnors och flickors behov. Insatsen är strukturerat som ett programstöd med två delar. I den första delen vidarebefordras medel till partnerorganisationer för att genomföra sina egna aktiviteter. I den andra delen genomför Kvinna till Kvinna aktiviteter för att öka deras partners totala kapacitet som kvinnorättighetsorganisationer och för att höja deras förmåga att samordna och driva den nationella dialogen.
Programmet delas in i fyra huvudmål:
- Partners är starkare, effektivare och arbetar mer strategiskt och samarbete - Förbättrat skydd mot könsbaserat våld med särskilt fokus på förebyggande - Rättighetsinnehavare och ansvarsbärare (duty bearers) har ökad förståelse och respekt för sexuell och reproduktiv hälsa och rättigheter (SRHR) - Förbättrat kvalitativt deltagande av kvinnor i beslutsfattande och konfliktlösning.

The overarching objective of the intervention is to contribute to strengthen the capacity and coordination of the women’s movement in Rwanda for more strategic interventions to enhance women’s voice and participation, freedom from violence and full enjoyment of human rights.
Kvinna till Kvinna has operated in Rwanda since 2017, when the Embassy decided to fund Kvinna till Kvinna’s first country programme in Rwanda. The overall aim of the programme has been to contribute towards a stronger and more connected women’s rights movement in Rwanda, working more effectively for gender equality and women’s empowerment. The new Kvinna till Kvinna’s proposal for 2021 – 2024 builds on the successes, challenges and lessons learned under the current phase while at the same time shifting the focus of the program to respond to socio-economic and political developments and emerging priorities to better respond to the needs of women and girls. The contribution is structured as a programme support with two pillars. The first pillar, which represents the majority of the programmes funding, is forwarded to partner organizations to implement their own activities. In the second pillar, Kvinna till Kvinna itself implement activities to increase their partners overall capacity as women’s rights organizations as well as their capacity to coordinate and pursue advocacy and national dialogue.
The key impact objectives are: - Partners are stronger, more effective and work more strategically - Improved protection from gender-based violence with a specific focus on prevention - Rights holders and duty bearers have an increased understanding and respect for Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR) - Enhanced qualitative participation of women in decision making and conflict resolution.

title.narrative: Grant Agreement between the Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency Sida, and Kvinna till Kvinna Foundation regarding Working together to reinforce change for the respect of women's rights in Rwanda 'Dufatanye', 2021-2024
Kvinna till Kvinna Rwanda phase II

description.narrative:
The Dufatanye programme ("Working together to reinforce change for the respect of women's rights in Rwanda", 20212024 with a 2025 extension) was implemented by The Kvinna till Kvinna Foundation - Rwanda in partnership with 11 women led civil society organisations (CSOs) and funded by Sida. The overall objective is to strengthen the capacity, coordination, and strategic impact of the women's movement in Rwanda across four primary outcome areas.
Outcome 1: Enabling Stronger, More Strategic & Collaborative Partner Organisations
Monitoring Evaluation Learning & Sustainability: In 2025 partners shifted from viewing Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL) merely as a reporting tool to utilizing MEL data strategically for external communication, visibility, and resource mobilization.
Governance & Regulatory Alignment: Rwanda Governance Board compelled all national and international NGOs to comply with registration requirements. Kvinna till Kvinna partners were supported in updating governance structures and institutional documents to comply with Rwanda's Law No.058/2024 governing NGOs.
Movement Building & Policy Influence: Convened the Rwanda Women's Alliance to adapt to shifting donor landscapes and influence national strategic priorities in the second phase of the National Strategy for Transformation (NST2).
Joint Advocacy: Kvinna till Kvinna Supported coalitions to submit the final Universal Periodic Review (UPR) shadow report (20212024) and held policy dialogues with the Economic Research Policy Network (EPRN) to promote women friendly financial products and services.
Outcome 2: Improved Protection from Gender-Based Violence (GBV)
2025 highlighted several evidence based judicial wins against GBV: Partners who included CERTA Foundation, Haguruka systematically integrated forensic evidence such as DNA testing into legal proceedings. This resolved long pending defilement backlogs some of them ranging over 18 months neutralized perpetrator denial, increased conviction rates, and secured awards for damages known as indishyi mbagamirabusembwa in Kinyarwanda.
Another success related to this outcome was enabling inclusive access to justice and psychosocial support to victims: Mobile legal clinics and trauma informed safe spaces e.g., HSMD's Uruganiriro (Dialogue) spaces and FADA's therapy groups enabled survivors, sex workers, and teen mothers to heal, build confidence, and report abuse.
Disability Integration: The program in 2025 expanded Rwandan Sign Language training for service providers, in partnership with Rwanda National Association of Deaf Women Association, significantly dismantling communication barriers for Deaf survivors accessing GBV and legal aid services.
Outcome 3: Increased Understanding and Respect for SRHR Policy Breakthrough.
There were coordinated advocacy efforts by programme partners and the Rwanda Young Women SRHR Network contributed to a major national policy milestone which was lowering the minimum age for independent access to SRHR information and services to 15 years.
Extensive & Inclusive Reach. The program Dufatanye reached 11,269 individuals directly and over 19,500 indirectly with SRHR information. Using adapted curricula and Sign Language, marginalized populations including Deaf youth gained equal access to bodily autonomy and sexual health education.
Norm Transformation: Under this goal in 2025 Dufatanye Employed Value Clarification and Action (VCAT) methodologies and community dialogues to shift deeply rooted social and religious stigmas around adolescent SRHR, menstrual health, and safe abortion.
Outcome 4: Qualitative Participation in Decision-Making & Conflict Resolution
Economic Autonomy & Climate Resilience: 2025 saw initiatives such as the VUGA UKIRE and Green Resilience Mentorship Programme which equipped women and teen mothers with climate smart agriculture skills, livestock, and savings mechanisms. Increased financial independence directly reduced household vulnerabilities and tolerance of financial dependence-linked abuse.
Community Leadership & Local Governance: The program enabled refresher leadership trainings for 176 Women Safe Space Facilitators and 55 Girl Champions equipped participants with storytelling, advocacy, and conflict-resolution skills. This translated into qualitative leadership gains, with participants being elected to local governance roles (such as Isibo leaders) and influencing local policy forums.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
